lines: Same passage. Two groups. A week later, one remembered way more.
In 2006, researchers had students learn a short passage.
Group one read it four times.
Group two read it once, then tested themselves three times.
A week later, the rereaders remembered forty percent. The testers? Sixty-one.
Pulling it out of your head is what makes it stick.
